name: Кощей Бессмертный и Златая цепь — 12 стадий (предложение)

mechanics.title: Objective-linked invulnerability
mechanics.summary: The boss ignores normal damage until a finite set of visible protection objectives is complete, then opens for a timed damage window.

mechanics.title: Burrow and emerge
mechanics.summary: The boss leaves direct interaction.

mechanics.title: Marked-area strike
mechanics.summary: The boss marks a region first and damages it after a delay.

mechanics.title: Beat-synced attack
mechanics.summary: An attack lands on a known position in an audible, visible rhythm whose clock persists across the boss's actions.

mechanics.title: Telegraph
mechanics.summary: A telegraph communicates an upcoming attack’s timing.

mechanics.title: Tower soak
mechanics.summary: A fixed point checks how many living players occupy it when the timer ends; a missed count changes the whole group's outcome.

mechanics.title: Encounter-specific tool
mechanics.summary: The encounter grants or activates a portable tool whose rule-specific action is unusually effective against this boss.

mechanics.title: Posture stagger gauge
mechanics.summary: Authored attacks and counters pressure a separate posture gauge; a break opens a bounded critical state that only an explicit finisher can consume.

mechanics.title: Ally theft and charm
mechanics.summary: The boss temporarily takes control of a player-owned helper or party member and turns that ally’s readable abilities against its former owner.

mechanics.title: Moving hazard
mechanics.summary: A persistent dangerous area travels through the arena, making the player plan against its future footprint rather than its starting position.

mechanics.title: Knockback
mechanics.summary: A hit displaces the player.

mechanics.title: Ability or healing lock
mechanics.summary: A marked contact temporarily rejects one named action while movement and the rest of the player kit remain available.

mechanics.title: Debuff handoff
mechanics.summary: A marked player transfers a harmful timed state through deliberate contact before it expires.

mechanics.title: Cover and line of sight
mechanics.summary: A physical object creates safety by blocking the line between a directional threat and the player.

mechanics.title: Baited self-hit
mechanics.summary: The player places or exposes a valid hazard, baits a committed boss action through it, and turns the boss's own resolution into damage or stagger.

mechanics.title: Decoy
mechanics.summary: The boss presents a convincing false target, so the player must identify which body can advance the fight before committing an attack.

mechanics.title: Teleport
mechanics.summary: A teleport removes the boss from one position and restores it at another without dangerous travel between the two points.

mechanics.title: Interruptible wind-up
mechanics.summary: A marked wind-up can be cancelled by a qualifying player action before its deadline.

mechanics.title: Homing projectile
mechanics.summary: A projectile adjusts its heading toward the player after launch.

mechanics.title: Escape phase
mechanics.summary: An escape phase gives the boss a destination and consequence outside ordinary combat. The player must interrupt, pursue, or accept the clearly stated result.

mechanics.title: Entity tether
mechanics.summary: A visible bond makes two entities' movement interdependent; crossing its stated limit changes the outcome for both.

mechanics.title: Nested / relocated arena
mechanics.summary: A relocated arena transfers the active boss fight into another playable space without ending or silently rebuilding the encounter.

mechanics.title: Boss as terrain
mechanics.summary: The player traverses the boss's body, and access to the damage point depends on a readable route and reliable holding rules.

mechanics.title: Charge
mechanics.summary: The boss aims, locks its direction, and charges forward. It cannot turn after the lock.

mechanics.title: Ground slam
mechanics.summary: The boss strikes the floor and sends a readable shockwave outward from the impact point.

mechanics.title: Invisibility
mechanics.summary: The boss hides its primary body signal while bounded environmental, audio, or particle traces preserve position and attack intent.

mechanics.title: Forced scrolling
mechanics.summary: Forced scrolling moves the camera or playable route independently of the player, so maintaining progress becomes a required part of the encounter.

mechanics.title: Partner revival
mechanics.summary: A surviving boss can restore a downed partner unless the cast is stopped or the pair is finished within the authored window.

mechanics.title: Ordered targets
mechanics.summary: The boss marks several targets and strikes them in a visible, committed order.

mechanics.title: Shockwave
mechanics.summary: An impact creates a threat that travels across a surface.

mechanics.title: Shrinking safe area
mechanics.summary: Danger advances inward or outward to reduce usable space.

mechanics.title: Environmental weapon
mechanics.summary: A fixed arena device must be reached and prepared; its resolved shot, not ordinary weapon damage, advances the encounter.

mechanics.title: Party split
mechanics.summary: The boss divides the group; both teams must finish their own task before everyone can reunite.

mechanics.title: Scanning beam
mechanics.summary: A sustained beam sweeps across space from one side to another.

mechanics.title: Pairing polarity
mechanics.summary: The boss marks four players; each receiving zone needs exactly one player of each polarity.

mechanics.title: Part break
mechanics.summary: A targeted boss component is destroyed, visibly disabling its associated attack.

mechanics.title: Gaze check
mechanics.summary: A marked source checks which way the player character faces when its gaze resolves.

mechanics.title: Hazard trail
mechanics.summary: Movement leaves a temporary dangerous path behind the boss or player.

mechanics.title: Platform destruction
mechanics.summary: The boss removes or disables pieces of traversable space.

mechanics.title: Grab
mechanics.summary: A grab replaces ordinary damage with capture.

mechanics.title: Pull
mechanics.summary: An announced inward force changes the player's movement and can draw their body into a dangerous center.

mechanics.title: Control mode shift
mechanics.summary: A control mode shift replaces the player's current movement or response grammar with another one during the same encounter.

mechanics.title: Projectile rally
mechanics.summary: Boss and player repeatedly return the same projectile until a missed response resolves the rally.

mechanics.title: Attack combination
mechanics.summary: Two or more familiar attacks are sequenced so the first response changes the starting conditions for the next.

mechanics.title: Wind-up
mechanics.summary: A wind-up is a readable pre-action state that gives the player time to identify and answer a pending attack.

mechanics.title: Landing jump
mechanics.summary: The boss leaps to a committed destination and turns the landing radius into a short radial threat.

mechanics.title: Target lock
mechanics.summary: The boss selects a player or position.

mechanics.title: Summon
mechanics.summary: The boss calls a limited group of helpers, changing priorities without flooding the arena.

mechanics.title: Directional shield
mechanics.summary: A raised shield blocks attacks from a fixed front sector, but an ordinary move around its edge leaves the boss exposed.

mechanics.title: Tankbuster and target handoff
mechanics.summary: A strong hit leaves its recipient vulnerable, so another defender must claim the boss before the repeat.

mechanics.title: Recovery
mechanics.summary: Recovery is the post-action interval before the boss may choose or start another action.

mechanics.title: Arc sweep
mechanics.summary: The boss anchors one end of an attack and sweeps a dangerous arc across the arena.

mechanics.title: Converging threats
mechanics.summary: Separate threats approach one another, narrowing a previously safe region and asking the player to leave it before the overlap.

mechanics.title: Weak point
mechanics.summary: Damage is concentrated on a specific body part.

mechanics.title: False death and return
mechanics.summary: The boss appears defeated, but encounter completion stays pending until a readable revival begins a new phase.

mechanics.title: Interface interaction
mechanics.summary: The boss can only be opened, weakened, or answered by using an input channel or system interface outside the player character's ordinary verbs.

mechanics.title: Loadout mirror
mechanics.summary: At a declared moment, the boss snapshots selected parts of the player’s build and converts them into a stable encounter package.

mechanics.title: Moveset shapeshifting
mechanics.summary: The boss changes between complete borrowed movesets, each with its own signals, attacks, movement rules, and recovery.

mechanics.title: Enrage
mechanics.summary: The boss enters a more demanding state after a threshold or time limit.

mechanics.title: Sound detection
mechanics.summary: The boss learns a location from audible events instead of reading the player's live position, making noise output part of movement and attack choices.

mechanics.title: Attack reflection
mechanics.summary: A guarded boss reverses an incoming attack, making its return path dangerous to the player.

mechanics.title: Survival phase
mechanics.summary: A survival phase advances when players endure a bounded sequence, timer, or objective rather than reducing boss health.

mechanics.title: Pacifist resolution
mechanics.summary: The encounter can end without emptying boss health when the player satisfies a visible nonviolent condition and commits to a separate spare action.

mechanics.title: Run-history manifestation
mechanics.summary: The encounter turns selected decisions accumulated before the boss into a stable set of enemies, allies, attacks, or rules.

mechanics.title: Persistent encounter progress
mechanics.summary: Completed encounter objectives survive player defeat, so a new attempt resumes from an explicit authored milestone instead of rebuilding the whole fight.
